arguments.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. DRAW a three-panel pencil staging storyboard for The Fall of a Quarter Star. Reference photos 1-4 control the dogs' anatomy; image 5 is ONLY smooth BODY FINISH calibration, never its Great Dane or park. Neet small tan short smooth dog fine legs full narrow torso large broad triangular ears tiny nub. Buddy full moderately elongated charcoal torso substantial legs real ground clearance projecting irregular cream moustache modest beard light brows and regional ear/paw furnishings. Panel A: sunny backyard, Neet barking at an opaque wooden fence with all four paws on ground, chest almost touching boards; Buddy beside him enthusiastically barking. No neighbor dogs visible through opaque fence. Plants/string lights in background. Panel B: night bedroom closet, Neet supported curled in dog bed at closet threshold, head raised and ears angled back in embarrassed retreat; Buddy stands beside outside the closet, looking at Neet. No humans needed in frame, no bug still present. Show believable spine, pelvis and limb ownership in curled Neet. Panel C: morning window, Neet upright meditating eyes closed seated, Buddy approaching from right chewing last little biscuit with crumbs below, three paws supporting and one front paw lifted; normal canine anatomy. Separate wide panels, room space, connected bodies, no dialogue or text. Draw all three actual scenes, not written instructions. Plain smooth torsos even in pencil; no curly hatch texture.
